summary: Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He served as Superintendent of the Western Circle at the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1917) and Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta.
Dewei Zhang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD from the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Jinhua Chen.
Dezhung Kunga Gyaltsen was a scholar who studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Gaton Ngawang Lekpa, Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and Ngawang Nyima. From 1960 to 1972, he participated in a research project at the University of Washington.

Dhammanandā is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe. She also studied under Viên Minh, Toshiichi Endo, and N. A. Jayawickrama.

Dhammapala is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, under Dhammasakkaro, and completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under K. L. Dhammajoti, later serving there as a guest assistant professor.

Dharmananda Kosambi was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Harvard University in 1926. He held posts at the University of Calcutta (~1906–1908), Harvard University (~1910–1931), Gujarat University (~1920–1928), and Saint Petersburg State University (~1929–1930).

Dhirendra Mohan Datta was a philosophy and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1921–1925). He held posts at Patna College in 1928 and the University of Minnesota from 1951 to 1952.
Dhirendra Sharma is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under David Friedman and Surendra Sharma.

Dhivan Thomas Jones is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He held an associate lecturer post at the Open University and a post at the University of Chester in 2019.
Di Luo is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Southern California under the supervision of Sonya S. Lee.

Diana L. Eck is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Smith College, SOAS University of London, and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. She held multiple professorships at Harvard University, where she is now Emerita.

Diana Lange is a Tibetology, Sinology, and history/archaeology scholar educated at Leipzig, Tibet University, Humboldt University, and EPHE. She held positions at several institutions, including Humboldt University of Berlin, where she became Professor of History and Cultures of Central Asia.

Diane A. Lichtenstein earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. She has served as an Adjunct Professor of Anthropology at Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art.

Diane Elizabeth Riggs is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned a PhD from UCLA under William M. Bodiford. She held positions at Kenyon College, Pepperdine University, and Western Michigan University.
Diane L. Howard is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who conducted graduate studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Graeme MacQueen.
Dickwela Piyananda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the Catholic University of America under the supervision of Siegfried A. Schulz.

Diego Loukota is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned an MA from Peking University and completed his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, in 2019.

Dieter B. Kapp was an Indology and linguistics scholar who earned his Dr. phil. from Heidelberg University under Hermann Berger. He taught at Heidelberg, Munich, and Berlin, and served as Director of the Institute for Indology and Tamil Studies at Cologne.
Dieter George was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who succeeded Wolfgang Voigt and held a post at the Prussian State Library from circa 1972 to 1985.
